# ALAS digitised wing sections.
#
# Format: '#' lines are comments. Each section is a line '@NAME', one
# description line, then 241 lines 'x z' in chords: Selig order (trailing
# edge, upper surface forward to the leading edge, lower surface aft to the
# trailing edge), 121 cosine-spaced stations per surface sharing the leading
# edge, leading edge at (0, 0), closed trailing edge at (1, 0).
#
# Method (all sections): each printed outline was traced on the page image
# (the darkest connected outline; per pixel column the outer edges of the
# upper and lower lines, per pixel row the nose; circle markers and the drawn
# chord-line dashes excluded), moved inward by half the measured line width
# to the line centre, and fitted with class-shape (CST, Kulfan) surfaces of
# degree 12 sharing one leading-edge coefficient, smoothed by the largest
# shape-curvature penalty that keeps the fit rms within 10 % of the
# unsmoothed fit. Chord: from the leading edge (vertex of the nose fitted as
# a parabola) to the trailing edge (747: the circle drawn there; DC-10: the
# pen tip), the trailing-edge height fitted to the converging lines. The
# drawing resolves the trailing-edge height to about 1 px, so the thin-airfoil
# c_m,c/4 of each camber line carries about +-0.01 (fit-order spread) to
# +-0.03 (1 px at the trailing edge). Thickness is the drawing's own; the
# presets rescale it to their documented t/c distributions. The nose radius
# is resolved where it exceeds the drawn line width (about 2 px): B747-Y109,
# B747-Y206 and DC10-BASIC. On B747-Y303, -Y400 and -Y500 the fitted radius
# (1.5, 1.0 and 0.6 px) is under the line width, so their nose curvature is
# the fit's, not the drawing's.
#
